  • Across the first nine months of 2026, Ziff Davis generated US$843.71 million in sales and US$618.03 million in net income, with very high basic and diluted earnings per share of US$17.22 that contrast sharply with the loss per share from continuing operations.

Ziff Davis Investment Narrative Recap

To stay invested in Ziff Davis, you need to believe the mix shift toward subscription, cybersecurity and martech can offset pressure on ad driven properties over time. The latest quarter adds tension to that view. Sales from continuing operations softened and the loss from those activities widened, which keeps the core profitability question very much open.

The key near term catalyst is how management deploys the sizeable cash and balance sheet capacity after the Connectivity sale, including acquisitions and buybacks. The biggest risk is that search driven and healthcare related media assets stay under pressure, so incremental capital fails to lift revenue or margins meaningfully against those headwinds.

RetailMeNot’s 20th National Cash Back Day event is a useful real time test of Ziff Davis’s Shopping and affiliate ecosystem. The promotion spans more than 3,500 retailers and offers elevated cash back rates, so it gives a live read on consumer engagement, advertiser appetite and how well the RetailMeNot platform converts traffic into monetizable transactions.

If these types of events keep users active and brands spending through the holidays, they can support the push toward more performance oriented digital advertising and e commerce that analysts have focused on as a catalyst. If uptake is weaker than hoped, it would underline the risk that Tech & Shopping properties remain under structural pressure from search changes and tougher competition.

data.title: What National Australia Bank Shares Weak Profit Means For Shareholders
data.description:
• National Australia Bank reported full year 2026 results with net interest income of A$18,494 million and net income of A$6,143 million, alongside lower earnings per share and higher credit impairment and restructuring related costs.
  • The bank paired weaker profit and increased loan loss provisions with an affirmed final dividend of A$0.85 per share, highlighting a tension between supporting shareholders and absorbing higher credit risk and expense pressures.
  • This article examines how National Australia Bank's investment narrative is affected by weaker profit driven by higher credit impairment charges.
Seize this chance to benchmark National Australia Bank against a curated group of banks and lenders that also face credit cycle pressure by scanning through 6 resilient stocks with low risk scores.

National Australia Bank Investment Narrative Recap

To stay invested in National Australia Bank, you need to be comfortable with a simple trade off. Management is leaning into a higher credit risk backdrop while still running a sizeable franchise built on business lending, deposits and a heavy spend on technology platforms. The latest result shows net income at A$6,143 million with weaker earnings per share and higher credit impairment, which keeps asset quality and cost control firmly in focus.

The key short term catalyst is whether credit losses and expenses settle into something more predictable so the existing digital and business banking projects can show through in profit. The biggest risk right now is that rising impairments and restructuring outlay keep net margins under pressure for longer, which could limit flexibility on growth and capital deployment.

The dividend affirmation at A$0.85 per share for the final period is the announcement that matters most here. It sits alongside higher credit provisions and restructuring charges, so it gives you a live test of how confident National Australia Bank is in its capital position while earnings are under pressure. For income focused holders, that combination will probably be front of mind.

This payout also interacts directly with the bank’s existing risks. If asset quality in business lending or consumer portfolios weakens further, or if expenses stay elevated as systems and workforce changes are rolled out, management may have less room to keep distributing capital at the same pace. That makes future updates on provisions, costs and restructuring progress critical catalysts to watch against the current dividend settings.

Analyst Scenario For National Australia Bank

Consensus expectations sketch a very specific path for National Australia Bank. Analysts are working off forecast revenue growth of 5.0% a year over the next three years and current earnings of about A$6.1b, with a view that profit margins could shift from 29.3% today to 33.4% by 2029 if execution lines up with the current plan around technology, deposits and business lending focus.

On those assumptions, the analyst group expects National Australia Bank's earnings to reach about A$8.1b by 2029, which is an increase of roughly A$2.0b from earnings today. That change implies a step up of around one third in profit over the period, so the projected improvement in margins does a lot of the heavy lifting in the story rather than only relying on volume or balance sheet expansion.

National Australia Bank's narrative projects revenues of about A$24.2b and earnings of about A$8.1b by 2029. This assumes 5.0% yearly revenue growth and an earnings increase of roughly A$2.0b from current earnings of about A$6.1b.

The valuation discussion then links these operating targets to what investors are currently willing to pay. The market price is A$39.25, while the analyst consensus target sits at A$38.46, only 2.1% lower. That narrow gap signals that, on average, analysts see the stock as broadly aligned with their implied fair value today, with the forward P/E on the 2029 earnings sitting at 18.5x compared with an estimated 19.8x on current earnings and 13.7x for the wider Australian banks sector.

Price targets around that A$38.46 average still span a wide band, from A$29.00 at the cautious end to A$48.50 at the more optimistic end. For you as a holder or potential investor, the useful exercise is to stress test the moving parts behind those numbers. That means asking whether a shift to A$24.2b of revenue, A$8.1b of earnings and a lower P/E multiple of 18.5x in 2029 feels reasonable given your view on credit risk, cost inflation and the pace of digital execution at National Australia Bank.

Exploring Other Perspectives

You can see how differently people read the same facts. The most cautious analysts worry that National Australia Bank’s higher technology and restructuring costs crowd out earnings, even before this profit drop and A$6,143 million net income update. They were already pencilling in about A$23.9b of 2029 revenue and A$8.0b of earnings. data.title: Does COG Financial Services (ASX:COG) Deserve A Spot On Your Watchlist?
data.description:
Investors are often guided by the idea of discovering 'the next big thing', even if that means buying 'story stocks' without any revenue, let alone profit. But the reality is that when a company loses money each year, for long enough, its investors will usually take their share of those losses. A loss-making company is yet to prove itself with profit, and eventually the inflow of external capital may dry up.

If this kind of company isn't your style, you like companies that generate revenue, and even earn profits, then you may well be interested in COG Financial Services (ASX:COG). Even if this company is fairly valued by the market, investors would agree that generating consistent profits will continue to provide COG Financial Services with the means to add long-term value to shareholders.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

COG Financial Services' Earnings Per Share Are Growing

If you believe that markets are even vaguely efficient, then over the long term you'd expect a company's share price to follow its earnings per share (EPS) outcomes. That makes EPS growth an attractive quality for any company. To the delight of shareholders, COG Financial Services has achieved impressive annual EPS growth of 39%, compound, over the last three years.
